newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader restricts free-market farm prices.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader restricts free-market farm prices.

text.p: Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko, already known for opposing market reforms in his former Soviet republic, has said farmers will need government permission to sell meat and eggs at free market prices.
Speaking on state television late on Monday, Lukashenko -- himself a former state farm chief -- also fixed the price of eggs at half the present market level.

The moves were clearly designed as vote-catchers ahead of a November 24 referendum in which the president is seeking to broaden his authority. The planned vote has attracted criticism at home and abroad.

"Collective farms are waiting but not selling livestock. They say prices are low. Commercial firms are selling livestock abroad," Lukashenko said after a tour of meat shops, a meat processing plant and a poultry farm.
He said farmers would need to apply for permission to sell meat and eggs at free prices at home or abroad. "We subsidised agriculture and we will not allow our money to go abroad."
Lukashenko fixed the price of 10 eggs at 12,000-16,000 Belarussian roubles -- almost half the market price.
Supplies of meat and eggs are becoming increasingly unreliable in Minsk, sparking fears of a return to Soviet days when shelves were sometimes bare for months on end.

Gennady Usyukevich, the head of parliament's agriculture committee, criticised Lukashenko's move. Parliament, which has proposed its own questions for the November 24 referendum, is fiercely opposed to Lukashenko's referendum plans.

"Agriculture now is in a worse state than it was under socialism. The state is simply forcing producers to sell goods at cheaper prices," Usyukevich said. "We need market prices -- only in this way will we solve the so-called food problem."
Lukashenko's decision contradicts demands from the International Monetary Fund which has urged the government to free prices.
The IMF has suspended its loan programme to Belarus pending faster reforms. Lukashenko has halted privatisation, imposed controls on banks and regulated the rouble rate.
